_readme: Hand-curated evidence for POS_ATOMIC_ACCEPTANCE_REGISTER.csv (generated by scripts/qa/generate-pos-acceptance-register.mjs). Every row not listed here defaults to UNVERIFIED — that is deliberate, not an oversight. Only requirement IDs this program has independently traced to real code AND a real, reproducible passing test appear below, matching the discipline scripts/validation/generate-crm-traceability.mjs already established for CRM. A feature being REAL/VERIFIED in POS_IMPLEMENTATION_TRACKER.md's feature-level gap matrix is NOT by itself evidence for any specific row here.

F292-BR-002.database_evidence: tenant.pos_return_payment_refunds (database/tenant/migrations/130_pos_return_refund_allocation_and_loyalty_snapshot.sql) -- trigger-enforced immutable (BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE raises an exception), matching every other POS evidence table's convention.
F292-BR-002.cross_module_integration: Consumed by accounting-posting.js's buildReturnJournalLines instead of reconstructing a proportional guess -- see F305-DATA-002.
F292-BR-002.positive_test: tests/integration/pos-financial-integrity-gaps-abc.test.mjs -- 'Gap B: FIRST partial return ... persists an exact per-payment refund record' and 'SECOND partial return ... still attributes correctly'
F292-BR-002.verification_result: 8/8 real-Postgres assertions passing (2026-09-19 session run, Prompt 2). Full existing 262-test real-Postgres suite re-passes unchanged.
F292-BR-002.notes: Two separate partial returns against the same split-tender sale were specifically tested to prove per-return attribution survives repeat returns -- exactly the case the prior reconstruction-based approach could not have gotten right.

F305-BR-002.database_evidence: tenant.pos_return_payment_refunds + pos_sales.loyalty_redemption_value_per_point_snapshot (migration 130) -- both immutable/append-only, corrections via new linked rows only.
F305-BR-002.positive_test: tests/integration/pos-financial-integrity-gaps-abc.test.mjs -- 'the loyalty program's rate is changed AFTER the sale -- the sale's own snapshot must not move'
F305-BR-002.verification_result: Confirmed the program's rate can be changed after a sale without altering that sale's own historical accrual valuation -- the specific historical-truth property this row requires.

F305-DATA-002.backend_function: recordReturnPaymentRefund (return-lifecycle.js) writes it; buildReturnJournalLines (accounting-posting.js) reads it.

F283-SEC-002.database_evidence: tenant.pos_payments (migration 048) and every later payment-related migration have no PAN/CVV/card-number column anywhere -- confirmed by direct schema grep across all tenant migrations this session.
F283-SEC-002.backend_function: sandbox-adapter.js (the only registered adapter) never receives or stores raw card data -- it only ever handles a provider_reference string.
F283-SEC-002.http_endpoint: POST /api/pos/payments/initiate (Zod schema accepts amount/method/metadata only, no card-data fields)
F283-SEC-002.verification_result: Verified by direct code/schema inspection this session (Prompt 2), not a new test -- the ABSENCE of a data path is what's being proven, which a positive test can't directly assert. No real (non-sandbox) provider adapter exists yet to verify this invariant against actual PCI-scope card data at all -- this row is only proven for the sandbox adapter's own reference-based flow.
F283-SEC-002.exact_gap: Not re-verified against a real, non-sandbox provider adapter (none exists in this codebase yet -- see F283/F284's own EXTERNAL ACTIVATION BLOCKED status in POS_IMPLEMENTATION_TRACKER.md).
F283-SEC-002.next_action: Re-verify this same invariant once a real provider adapter is built.
F283-SEC-002.notes: Marked PASS for the sandbox-only architecture as it exists today; the real, uncontrolled risk (a genuine third-party SDK or hosted-field integration leaking raw card data) can only be assessed once real provider code exists.

F275-CAP-001.database_evidence: tenant.sales_pricing_rules (database/tenant/migrations/008_sales_module.sql) -- reused, not a new POS-owned table.
F275-CAP-001.http_endpoint: POST /api/pos/carts/[id]/lines (existing route, unchanged contract; pricing now customer-sensitive under the hood)
F275-CAP-001.frontend_evidence: apps/web/src/features/pos/checkout/screens/PosCheckoutScreen.tsx -- unchanged UI, correct price now flows through automatically once a customer is selected
F275-CAP-001.security_permission_evidence: No new permission required; reuses the existing pos.sale.create gate on cart mutations.
F275-CAP-001.cross_module_integration: Reuses Sales' own authoritative pricing-rule table and exact adjustment semantics (services/api/src/modules/sales/index.js:334-364) -- no second POS-owned pricing master created, per the explicit instruction.
F275-CAP-001.positive_test: tests/integration/pos-customer-pricing-f275.test.mjs -- 'a customer with a discount_percent rule gets the adjusted price', 'a customer with a fixed_rate rule gets exactly that rate', and (added this session) 'GAP CLOSURE: the legacy flat-lines completePointOfSale path now also applies a customer's discount_percent rule'
F275-CAP-001.negative_test: tests/integration/pos-customer-pricing-f275.test.mjs -- 'no customer selected: plain price-list rate applies', 'a customer with NO pricing rule still gets the plain price-list rate', 'the discount customer's rule is scoped to its own item -- a DIFFERENT item is unaffected', and (added this session) 'GAP CLOSURE: the legacy flat-lines path leaves a walk-in (no customer) sale unaffected'
F275-CAP-001.verification_result: 9/9 real-Postgres assertions passing (up from 7/7, this session); full existing 269-test real-Postgres suite re-passes unchanged (no regression).
F275-CAP-001.notes: This is the specific gap the Prompt 1 brief named by number and asked to investigate; confirmed still open by direct code read before any fix was written. UPDATE (comprehensive completion pass, later session): the legacy flat-lines completePointOfSale path (sale-completion.js's resolvePointOfSaleUnitPrice) was previously disclosed as NOT fixed here, on the assumption it was a deprecated/soon-to-be-removed path. Re-examination found it is NOT dead code -- it is what POST /api/pos/sales (a real, customerId-accepting HTTP endpoint) and offline-sync's own sale-completion step both complete through. applyCustomerPricingRules is now exported from cart-pricing.js and reused (not duplicated) by resolvePointOfSaleUnitPrice. Both entry points now apply customer-sensitive pricing; this row's prior disclosed gap is closed.

F289-BR-002.database_evidence: tenant.pos_receipt_print_events (database/tenant/migrations/129_pos_receipt_print_events.sql) -- trigger-enforced immutable (BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE raises an exception), matching every other POS evidence table's convention.
F289-BR-002.frontend_evidence: apps/web/src/features/pos/receipts/screens/PosReceiptScreen.tsx -- badge now reads real print-event history
F289-BR-002.security_permission_evidence: requirePosAccess(client, session, 'pos.view', { mutation: true }) -- billing-write-gated like every other POS mutation; verify:route-security and the SP011 billing-mutation-wiring integration test both confirmed this route is accounted for.
F289-BR-002.positive_test: Migration applied and verify:db passed (129 tenant migrations). Route/typecheck/lint/build all clean.
F289-BR-002.browser_test: apps/web/e2e/pos-checkout.spec.ts -- asserts the server-derived badge ('Not yet printed' before any print, 'Printed — original' after) and a real pos_receipt_print_events row queried directly from Postgres. Confirmed passing this session (Prompt 2) after root-causing and fixing the E2E suite's six real underlying defects (see commit 60221917) -- 11/11 across the full core POS E2E batch, run together.
F289-BR-002.verification_result: Full end-to-end browser journey independently confirmed green: sale completion -> receipt screen -> Print click -> badge flips to 'Printed — original' -> a real immutable pos_receipt_print_events row exists in Postgres with print_type='original'.
F289-BR-002.notes: Prompt 1's handoff left this row's browser evidence unconfirmed, citing a 'pre-existing environment flake.' Prompt 2 investigated that claim directly (network capture, DB inspection, page snapshots) rather than accepting it, and found six concrete, fixable root causes, none of them a genuine flake -- see the commit message for the full list.

F289-CAP-001.exact_gap: The full CAP-001 wording is 'idempotent receipt rendering/printing/reprint with original-vs-copy marking AND device failure recovery.' Original-vs-copy marking is now real (see F289-BR-002). Device failure recovery (detecting/recovering from an actual printer failure) is NOT implemented and cannot be from a browser -- window.print() has no printer-status callback in any browser. This is an honest, permanent limitation of browser-based printing, not a code gap this program can close without native/kiosk printer integration (a genuine external/hardware dependency).
F289-CAP-001.next_action: If native kiosk printer integration is ever in scope, build real print-outcome callback wiring then. Until then, this requirement's device-failure-recovery clause should be explicitly marked NOT_APPLICABLE with this same justification rather than left ambiguously PARTIAL forever.
F289-CAP-001.notes: Deliberately NOT marked PASS despite the fix landing -- the requirement text is broader than what was built, and marking it PASS would violate this program's own anti-fraud instruction.

F301-FLOW-002.database_evidence: tenant.operation_idempotency (existing shared table, reused -- no new table)
F301-FLOW-002.http_endpoint: POST /api/pos/shifts (idempotencyKey now a required Zod field)
F301-FLOW-002.frontend_evidence: apps/web/src/features/pos/overview/screens/PosOverviewScreen.tsx -- openShiftIdempotencyKey state, rotated on success, matching the existing recordPosCashMovement UI pattern exactly
F301-FLOW-002.positive_test: tests/integration/pos-shift-open-idempotency-f301.test.mjs -- 'a retry with the SAME idempotency key and the SAME payload replays the original shift -- exactly one row persisted'
F301-FLOW-002.negative_test: tests/integration/pos-shift-open-idempotency-f301.test.mjs -- 'the SAME idempotency key with a DIFFERENT payload is rejected' (asserts IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED) and 'a replay attempt by an UNAUTHORIZED user is stopped by authorization, never returns the original shift'
F301-FLOW-002.concurrency_retry_test: tests/integration/pos-shift-open-idempotency-f301.test.mjs -- 'CONCURRENCY: two genuinely simultaneous requests with the identical key/payload create exactly ONE shift' -- a real two-Postgres-connection race (same pattern as the established stock-race test), not a single-connection simulation.
F301-FLOW-002.verification_result: 5/5 real-Postgres assertions passing (dedicated new suite, this session). Full existing 276-test real-Postgres suite re-passes unchanged (no regression).
F301-FLOW-002.notes: Closes the exact gap this row's own prior entry disclosed: same-key/same-payload replay, same-key/different-payload rejection, genuine two-connection concurrency, and authorization-enforced-on-replay are now each proven directly through openShift itself, not just inferred from the shared primitive's generic coverage plus a passing regression sweep.

F292-DATA-002.database_evidence: tenant.pos_return_payment_refunds -- now backfilled (database/tenant/migrations/132_pos_historical_refund_allocation_backfill.sql) for every historical (pre-migration-130) return whose allocation is unambiguously recoverable from other real evidence (100% cash, refund_total exactly equal to the persisted cash-refund movement total, zero non-cash tender legs on the underlying sale).
F292-DATA-002.backend_function: recordReturnPaymentRefund (return-lifecycle.js, real-time path, unchanged); migration 132 (one-time backfill, data only, no application code change).
F292-DATA-002.cross_module_integration: buildReturnJournalLines (accounting-posting.js) now reads exact persisted evidence for these historical rows instead of falling back to proportional reconstruction at every posting run.
F292-DATA-002.verification_result: Investigated directly against the live database (Prompt 3, Section 6D): found 4 real historical returns lacking a persisted allocation row, all 100%-cash with zero non-cash legs (an unambiguous, not estimated, allocation) -- backfilled and confirmed queryable via the exact query accounting-posting.js uses. Found 53 additional returns still lacking a row; sampled and confirmed these reference organization_ids with NO corresponding public.organizations row (orphaned test-run debris, unreachable via any tenant-scoped read since RLS requires a live organization context) -- deliberately left untouched rather than guessed at. verify:db clean at 132 tenant migrations; full real-Postgres suite (276/276) and test:api (1112/1112) re-pass unchanged after applying the migration.
F292-DATA-002.exact_gap: The 53 orphaned rows are permanently unrecoverable (their organizations no longer exist) and were deliberately left as-is rather than fabricated -- not a code gap, a consequence of the shared dev database's own test-run history.
F292-DATA-002.next_action: None for the 4 real rows (closed). The 53 orphaned rows are not actionable and not reachable by any live code path; no further action needed.
F292-DATA-002.notes: Deliberately did NOT attempt to reconstruct an estimated split for any ambiguous historical return (one with multiple non-cash legs) -- writing an ESTIMATE into a table whose entire purpose is EXACT evidence would make estimated data indistinguishable from genuine ground truth to a future auditor, which this program's own anti-fabrication rule forbids. accounting-posting.js's existing runtime fallback continues to serve any such case correctly and transparently.

F274-CALC-001.database_evidence: tenant.price_list_items.variant_id (database/tenant/migrations/131_pos_variant_specific_pricing.sql), indexed for the variant-preferring lookup.
F274-CALC-001.backend_function: resolveUnitPrice (cart path) / resolvePointOfSaleUnitPrice (legacy flat-lines path), services/api/src/modules/point-of-sale/assortment-pricing-customer-and-cart/{cart-pricing,sale-completion}.js -- both use the same variant-preferring price-list query and the shared fixed-point core/decimal.js primitives for the resulting unit price, never native Number arithmetic.
F274-CALC-001.cross_module_integration: Reuses Sales' own tenant.price_list_items table (adds a column, not a second POS-owned pricing table) -- the same reuse discipline F275's own fix follows for tenant.sales_pricing_rules.
F274-CALC-001.positive_test: tests/integration/pos-variant-specific-pricing-f274.test.mjs -- 'the Large variant resolves its own specific rate (130), not the generic item rate (100)' (cart path) and 'the legacy flat-lines completePointOfSale path also resolves the Large variant's own rate (130)' (legacy path)
F274-CALC-001.negative_test: tests/integration/pos-variant-specific-pricing-f274.test.mjs -- 'the Small variant (no rate row of its own) correctly falls back to the generic item rate (100)' and 'a plain line with NO variant selected still gets the generic rate (100), never the Large-specific one'
F274-CALC-001.verification_result: 7/7 real-Postgres assertions passing across both entry points; full existing 271-test real-Postgres suite re-passes unchanged.
F274-CALC-001.notes: A variant-specific row wins over the item-generic one via ORDER BY (variant_id IS NOT NULL) DESC when both exist for the same item/quantity tier; a plain no-variant line never matches a variant-specific row (variant_id=$N OR variant_id IS NULL, with $N NULL for a plain line).

F274-VAL-001.database_evidence: tenant.item_variants (existing table) -- FK from pos_sale_lines.variant_id stops a nonexistent variant id; this row's own gap was a real, EXISTING variant belonging to the wrong item passing that FK check regardless.
F274-VAL-001.backend_function: resolveItemAndVariant (cart-pricing.js, pre-existing) and the newly added equivalent inline check in completePointOfSale's line loop (sale-completion.js) -- both reject a variant that doesn't belong to the claimed item_id, isn't status='active', or belongs to a different company.
F274-VAL-001.negative_test: tests/integration/pos-variant-specific-pricing-f274.test.mjs -- 'GAP CLOSURE: the legacy flat-lines path rejects a real variant that belongs to a DIFFERENT item' (asserts POS_SALE_VARIANT_NOT_FOUND)
F274-VAL-001.verification_result: Confirmed via real PostgreSQL: a real, active, correctly-company-scoped variant belonging to a second, unrelated item is rejected when supplied against the first item's line.
F274-VAL-001.exact_gap: The cart path's own resolveItemAndVariant validation predates this session and was not independently re-tested for the cross-item-mismatch case specifically (only the legacy path got a new dedicated negative test this session) -- believed equivalent by direct code read (identical query shape), not independently proven by a cart-path test of its own.
F274-VAL-001.next_action: Add the same cross-item-mismatch negative test for the cart path (addPosCartLine) for full parity with the legacy-path coverage.
F274-VAL-001.notes: Found while closing F274's pricing gap on the legacy path: the legacy path recorded line.variantId with zero application-level validation that it belonged to the claimed item -- a DB FK alone does not catch a real variant attached to the wrong item.

F302-CALC-001.database_evidence: tenant.pos_shifts.cash_variance (existing column, now written with correct decimal precision instead of native-float-derived text)
F302-CALC-001.backend_function: closeShift, services/api/src/modules/point-of-sale/cash-shift-day-end-and-reconciliation/shift-operations.js -- now uses decimal()/sub()/asDatabaseDecimal() from core/decimal.js instead of native Number arithmetic
F302-CALC-001.cross_module_integration: F303's own day-end Z report and F304's own reconciliation both reuse this same cash_variance figure -- fixing its precision at the source benefits both without touching either.
F302-CALC-001.positive_test: tests/integration/pos-cash-movements-and-shift-close-f299-f302.test.mjs -- pre-existing suite, re-passes with exact decimal values after the arithmetic rewrite (this IS the regression proof; no new dedicated test for the specific 'this used to be float, now it's exact' distinction was added, since the pre-existing test already asserts exact string-formatted decimal values and passing it at all already proves fixed-point precision).
F302-CALC-001.verification_result: 254/254 full real-Postgres suite passing, including this file, after the rewrite.
F302-CALC-001.notes: A secondary, positive side effect: decimal() throws on non-numeric input instead of the old Number(garbage) silently producing NaN, which would previously have been written to the database as literal text 'NaN' (Postgres numeric columns do accept the special value 'NaN'). Not separately tested this session; disclosed as an unverified-but-believed-true improvement, not claimed as independently proven.
